correctness.rationale: For N=3k+1, both endpoints indeed have potential 1/2 and the palindromic interior has M=3q−2, q=2k+1. The continuant recurrence gives d_(3r)=(-2)^r, d_(3r+1)=2(-2)^r and d_(3r+2)=0. Substituting suffix/prefix minors in the inverse gives geometric decay in |i−j| and a q-independent operator norm bound; therefore the interior stays invertible on a fixed interval. The diagonal Green entry is 1/2, the off-diagonal corner is 2^(−q), and directly summing the squared corner column gives (2/3)−(5/3)4^(−q). Thus the Schur diagonal vanishes at zero with derivative −(5/3)(1−4^(−q)), while the off-diagonal is −2^(−q). The Schur derivative is bounded above by −I, forcing one root per reflection channel at distance at most 2^(−q), with opposite signs and no other roots in the fixed interval. Uniform resolvent bounds control the diagonal Taylor remainder; the inverse determinant expression has logarithmic derivative O(q), which controls the off-diagonal on this scale. Both energy errors are O(q4^(−q)), giving ±(3/10)4^(−k)+O(k16^(−k)) and the reciprocal 10/3. Independent integer Sturm inertia checks and tight bisection corroborated the isolation and both scaled constants at k=3,6,12,20,32.
residual_risks: Finite numerical corroboration is not the uniform spectral gap proof; the proof is specific to the given potential and cutoff residue.

value.rationale: The phase and model are motivated by an established failure of finite-section inversion, not arbitrarily tuned. Turning qualitative instability into a sharp inverse-norm law, and identifying precisely two exponentially small eigenvalues of opposite signs rather than a collapsing bulk gap, gives necessary conditioning information about this benchmark. The exact coefficient and remainder distinguish this result from a numerical observation or a monodromy bound.
residual_risks: No robustness with respect to changes of boundary phase, potential or boundary conditions is asserted.
